Case Study: A Delivery Drone Lifts Off

Read the passage carefully, then answer the 5 MCQs in the test below.

A courier company tests a delivery drone that lifts off from a rooftop launch pad, which the flight computer treats as the origin. After a short programmed hop the drone hovers at a point whose position vector, measured in hundreds of metres, is \vec a=2\hat i+3\hat j+6\hat k, where \hat i, \hat j and \hat k point east, north and vertically up. The navigation unit repeatedly needs three things from this single vector: the straight-line distance from the pad, the pure direction of travel with the distance stripped away, and the angles the flight path makes with the three axes. Before trusting the software, the engineer works these out by hand — the magnitude, the unit vector, and the direction cosines — and checks the identity that the squares of the three direction cosines always add to one.
